newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to sign Greenland exploration partnership.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to sign Greenland exploration partnership.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap ASA will sign a licence partnership on Thursday for the Fylla area off the west Greenland port of Nuuk with Phillips Petroleum Co, Danish Dopas and local company Nunaoil, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said.

Statoil said the group would like to implement plans soon for exploration drilling. The first step would be to install equipment in 1,100 metres of water on Fylla to measure currents and temperatures over the next six to 12 months.
The licence covers 9,487 square km, corresponding to about 17 Norwegian North Sea blocks.
"We plan to shoot seismic next summer and will charter a rig at a later date," Vidar Larsen, exploration manager at Statoil Denmark, told the newsletter.
"An application for an exploration and production licence was lodged by the Statoil group on February 29, but dealing with it has taken a long time," he said.
The Fylla acreage is the first to be licensed off Greenland since the 1970s. Seismic surveys in the area have revealed interesting geological structures that could hold oil and gas, Statoil said.
